job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today in our computer class, our teacher explained how to stay safe online. I learned that a strong password should be long and complex, not just my pet’s name or birthday, because those are easy for others to guess. Even if I use two-step verification with an OTP, I still need a strong password to keep my account secure. My teacher also warned us about phishing scams. Just because a message has a bank’s logo or claims I won a prize, it does not mean it is real; scammers use these tricks to steal information. I was surprised to learn that an OTP is a secret key that should never be shared with anyone, not even a best friend or someone claiming to be from a bank. Also, I realized that Incognito mode is not a shield against viruses or fake websites; it only stops my browsing history from being saved on the computer. Finally, we discussed that if I am ever bullied online, I must not stay silent or reply in anger; instead, I should report the user and talk to an adult immediately. It is important to remember that reporting online fraud is actually useful, as authorities can help track these criminals. I feel much more confident about navigating the internet safely now.

items.evidence: I learned that a strong password should be long and complex, not just my pet’s name or birthday, because those are easy for others to guess.
items.q: Meena's password is her dog's name plus her birthday. What is the problem with it?
options: It is easy for others to guess
It is missing a capital letter and number
It should swap letters for symbols like @
It is too long and hard to type
items.explain: Pet names and birthdays are easy for others to guess, so they make weak passwords.

wrong.why: thinks one capital and one number make a password strong
thinks symbol swaps make a password strong
reverses the advice that passwords should be long

items.evidence: Even if I use two-step verification with an OTP, I still need a strong password to keep my account secure.
items.q: Sohan turns on two-step verification with an OTP. What should he now do about his password?
options: Keep it long and complex anyway
Make it short, as the OTP protects him
Use his pet's name so it is easy
Remove it, as the OTP is enough
items.explain: Even with an OTP, a strong password is still needed to keep the account secure.

wrong.why: thinks the OTP makes password strength unimportant
thinks a pet's name is safe because only he knows it
thinks two-step verification replaces the password

items.evidence: Just because a message has a bank’s logo or claims I won a prize, it does not mean it is real; scammers use these tricks to steal information.
items.q: A message with a bank's logo says Priya won a prize. What does this prove?
options: It proves nothing; scammers use such tricks
It proves the bank really sent it
It proves she won, since they have her number
It proves the bank wants to reward her
items.explain: Logos and prize claims do not make a message real; scammers use them to steal information.

wrong.why: trusts a message because it has a logo
thinks knowing her number makes the prize real
takes the message's claim at face value

items.evidence: I was surprised to learn that an OTP is a secret key that should never be shared with anyone, not even a best friend or someone claiming to be from a bank.
items.q: Who can Kavya safely tell her OTP to?
options: No one, not even a bank caller
Her best friend, whom she fully trusts
A bank caller who knows her name
Anyone, if the OTP is quite short
items.explain: An OTP is a secret key that must never be shared, even with friends or bank callers.

wrong.why: thinks close friends can be trusted with secrets
trusts a caller who knows her name
thinks only long OTPs are dangerous to share

items.evidence: Also, I realized that Incognito mode is not a shield against viruses or fake websites; it only stops my browsing history from being saved on the computer.
items.q: Aman opens a strange website in Incognito mode. How does this mode help him?
options: Stops his history being saved on that computer
Protects his computer from any viruses
Hides his activity from websites and his provider
Warns him if the website is fake
items.explain: Incognito only stops browsing history being saved; it does not block viruses or fake websites.

wrong.why: thinks Incognito is a shield against viruses
thinks Incognito makes him anonymous online
